web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What growth and margin trajectory does ₹438.90 already price in, and how does IGIL stack up against Indian jewelry and certification peers?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a toll-booth compounds at 25% with 69% ROCE, the market rarely puts it on the clearance rack—your job is to measure whether expectations have outrun reality.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.text: Deconstructing Today's Price: ₹438.90 (₹18,967 Cr Market Cap)

web_blocks.html: At the November 13, 2026 NSE close of ₹438.90, IGIL carries a market cap of ₹18,967 Cr [1][17]. The stock trades at 28.5x Screener P/E (29.48x TradingView TTM P/E) and 10.83x Price-to-Book, with a 0.58% dividend yield [1][17]. For a franchise earning 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE with 57.7%–61% operating margins, a sub-30x multiple is modest. That discount reflects market caution over falling wholesale LGD prices and Blackstone's 76.55% stake ahead of the December 2027 MPS deadline [1][14][17].

web_blocks.text: Reverse DCF: What Today's ₹18,967 Cr Valuation Assumes

web_blocks.html: Let us invert the valuation to see what the market already expects. With net cash and minimal debt (Debt/Equity 0.09x), Enterprise Value sits near ₹18,500–₹18,967 Cr [1][17]. Using an 11.0% cost of equity, a 5.0% terminal growth rate, and ~₹550–₹600 Cr normalized FCF, ₹438.90 implies 13.5%–15.0% annual FCF compounding over ten years at 52%–55% EBITDA margins.

Now compare that hurdle against real execution. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 15% to 27%+ after Q2 FY27 revenue grew +31% YoY and PAT rose +43% YoY [4][5]. If IGIL compounds earnings at 18%–22% over the next five years, it will easily outgrow its 28.5x multiple. Conversely, if fee rebates push EBITDA margins below 48% and growth slows to 10%–12%, fair value drops toward ₹310–₹340.

web_blocks.text: Peer Comparison: Jewelry Ecosystem & Asset-Light Rating Toll-Booths

web_blocks.html: IGIL has no pure-play listed gem lab peer in India because GIA and HRD are non-profits. We benchmark it against two groups: Indian jewelry players (GOLDIAM, TITAN, KALYANKJIL) and asset-light rating toll-booths (CRISIL) [17][18][19][20][21].

The valuation gap across peers is clear. GOLDIAM trades at 20.6x P/E with 25.8% ROCE, reflecting manufacturing working-capital cycles [18]. TITAN (60.5x P/E, 20.5% ROCE) and KALYANKJIL (45.7x P/E, 21.2% ROCE) command steep retail multiples [19][20]. Even CRISIL trades at 35.5x P/E on 32.6% ROCE [21]. IGIL offers 69.2% ROCE at 28.5x P/E [1][17].
On FY28E PAT of ₹770–₹800 Cr, a flat 28.5x multiple supports our Base Target of ₹520.00 (+18.5% from CMP). A re-rating toward CRISIL's 35.5x multiple would lift fair value above ₹635.

Valuation Upgrade / Downgrade Trigger: Upgrade Base Target above ₹560 if implied revenue per report holds flat YoY through Q4 FY27 while EBITDA margins stay above 57%. Cut fair value toward ₹310 if ASP drops >10% YoY or EBITDA margins break below 48%.

web_blocks.title: VALUATION TAKEAWAY: QUALITY AT A FAIR MULTIPLE, NOT ON SALE
paragraphs: Over 12–18 months, IGIL is attractively valued relative to its 69.2% ROCE and 27%+ growth guidance (Base Target ₹520.00). After a +38.28% one-month rally, however, the margin of safety is far better at ₹375–₹395 than at ₹438.90.

book_paragraphs: Once we lock our price-blind verdict—that IGIL is a genuine Compounder Pass with 69% ROCE and 57%-plus operating margins—we finally open the market screen. As of the November 13, 2026 close, IGIL trades at ₹438.90, giving the entire global franchise a market capitalization of ₹18,967 crore and a trailing P/E multiple of 28.5 times.

Pause and ask yourself why a debt-free toll-booth growing top-line revenue at 31% year-on-year in its latest quarter trades at 28.5 times earnings, while Titan commands 60.5 times, Kalyan Jewellers trades at 45.7 times, and even slower-growing rating agency CRISIL sits at 35.5 times. The market is not blind. It is charging a clear discount for two anxieties: first, the fear that falling wholesale lab-grown diamond prices will eventually force certification fee cuts; and second, the certainty that Blackstone's 76.55% promoter stake must be pared down below 75% by December 2027.

book_subsections.title: Running the Reverse DCF on ₹438.90
paragraphs: Instead of guessing a target price out of thin air, let us invert the math and ask what ₹438.90 already assumes. With net cash on the balance sheet and minimal capital expenditure, discounting future free cash flows at an 11% cost of equity and a 5% terminal rate shows that today's share price requires roughly 14% annual free cash flow growth over the next ten years at mid-50s EBITDA margins.

That is a remarkably reasonable hurdle for a company that just raised FY27 revenue guidance to 27%+ following GIA's retreat from granular lab-grown 4Cs grading. If IGIL compounds earnings at 18% to 20% over the next three years, a ₹520 base valuation (roughly 29 times FY28 earnings) is well supported by cash generation alone, without needing any speculative multiple expansion. Yet if you pay ₹438.90 today after a 38% one-month rally, your near-term upside is only 18.5% while your drawdown risk back to the 200-day moving average is over 21%.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: VALUATION VS. ENTRY TIMING
callouts.text: A great business at a fair price can still be a poor short-term entry if the stock has just sprinted 38% in thirty days. Valuation tells you what to own; the tape tells you when to step up.

book_subsections.title: Why IGIL Trades Cheaper Than Titan, Kalyan, and CRISIL
paragraphs: Compare IGIL side-by-side against the four peers in our snapshot table, and a puzzle immediately jumps off the page. Titan trades at 60.5 times earnings with 20.5% ROCE. Kalyan Jewellers trades at 45.7 times earnings with 21.2% ROCE. CRISIL—an asset-light credit rating toll-booth—trades at 35.5 times earnings with 32.6% ROCE. Meanwhile, IGIL generates 69.2% ROCE and 55.8% ROE, yet trades at just 28.5 times earnings.

Why the discount? First, IGIL has less than two years of public-market seasoning since its December 2024 IPO, whereas Titan and CRISIL are multi-decade institutional darlings. Second, Goldiam International's 20.6x multiple reminds investors that the broader diamond-export ecosystem has historically been cyclical and working-capital heavy—even though IGIL itself carries zero inventory. As IGIL strings together several clean quarters post-GIA's October 2025 shift and proves its ASP resilience, that 28.5x multiple has room to re-rate toward 32x–35x.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity Check: What Happens If Multiples Expand or Compress?
paragraphs: Let us run a quick mental sensitivity check on our ₹520 base target. Suppose IGIL compounds net profit at roughly 22% annually over the next two years—conservative relative to Q2 FY27's 43% PAT surge and 27%+ full-year revenue guidance. Even if the stock receives zero multiple expansion and stays pinned at today's 28.5 times earnings, earnings growth alone carries the share price into the ₹510 to ₹530 band over 12 to 18 months.

If the market eventually awards IGIL a 33x to 35x multiple—still below CRISIL's 35.5x and far below Titan's 60.5x—the stock reaches ₹600+. Conversely, if LGD fee compression knocks margins down by 800 basis points and the multiple compresses to 20x, the downside sits near ₹310. That clear boundary between ₹310 bear value and ₹600 bull value is why entry price matters so much.

book_subsections.title: The PEG & Cash-Yield Reality Check
paragraphs: When you strip away market noise and look at IGIL through a simple PEG and free-cash-flow yield lens, the valuation picture snaps into focus. At 28.5 times trailing earnings for a business compounding normalized profits above 22% annually, IGIL trades at a PEG ratio just above 1.2 times—while generating a 3.0% to 3.3% unlevered free-cash-flow yield.

Compare that to paying 45x to 60x earnings for downstream jewelry retailers whose free cash flow is constantly tied up in gold and diamond inventory across hundreds of new store openings. Over a three-to-five-year horizon, IGIL's superior cash conversion gives it a decisive compounding edge once entered at the right technical price.
